phase: P01 (with P08 webhook boundary pulled forward for severity)
scope: Traced: UserRole enum vs role presets; every event-bus subscription vs raised event types; ResponseHelper.unauthorized callers; Stripe webhook controller/route/provider/raw-body declaration
reviewed_without_change: error-response/validation/authentication helpers: consistent with prior P01-24..26 contracts; Prisma codes outside P2002/P2025/P2003 map to redacted 500 (policy for P2000/P2034 left to owning phases).
Role presets match all non-GUEST UserRole enum values.
Persistence base/helper: unchanged contracts from P01-27/28.
Event bus: the only production subscription ('stock.added') matches StockAddedEvent.eventType and the stock repository dispatches through the bus.

findings.problem: When STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET was absent (allowed by configuration whenever STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is set), the webhook skipped signature verification and trusted the request body. Any caller sending any Stripe-Signature value and a payment_intent.succeeded body could authorize and capture a payment intent; customers receive their own Stripe intent ID from create-intent.
findings.change: Fail closed: with no signing secret every event is refused with 503 WEBHOOK_NOT_CONFIGURED before any payment lookup. Stripe configuration is injected from validated config (ContainerConfig.stripe) instead of getStripeConfig()/process.env.
findings.verification: Controller baseline: forged event returned 200 and captured; fixed: 503 with no payment calls, also when a signing secret exists only in the ambient environment. Real createServer route: 503.

findings.problem: The webhook route requested config.rawBody, but nothing populated request.rawBody (only a type declaration existed). Signature verification therefore received undefined and every genuine signed Stripe event was rejected, so payments were never captured through the webhook.
findings.change: Raw-body plugin replaces the default JSON parser with Fastify's own getDefaultJsonParser('error','error') and additionally keeps the exact buffer on routes with config.rawBody; registered right after config.
findings.verification: Real createServer route baseline: correctly signed event 401; fixed: 200. Parser cases: exact bytes kept (incl. charset), no raw body on other routes, prototype/constructor poisoning and invalid JSON 400, empty body 400, body limit 413.

findings.problem: Signature failures returned 401 without an authentication challenge (Stripe expects 400 for verification failure); ResponseHelper.unauthorized omitted the WWW-Authenticate header required on every 401 by RFC 9110 section 15.5.2; non-JSON payloads reached verification without raw bytes.
findings.change: Signature failure and missing raw payload return 400; ResponseHelper.unauthorized (now used only by checkout bearer checks) sends the Bearer challenge.
findings.verification: Forged, wrong-secret and wrong-bytes signatures 400 with no WWW-Authenticate; text/plain payload 400; helper challenge asserted (baseline failed).

tests.baseline: With a no-op raw-body stand-in: 7 of 13 initial cases failed (valid signature 401; forged unsigned event 200 + capture). Helper challenge assertion failed before the fix. One later test assumed text/plain would be rejected with 415; Fastify parses text/plain, so the expectation was corrected to the controller's 400 guard.
tests.coverage: raw-body.ts 100%; response.helper.ts 100% lines / 97.29% branches; stripe-webhook.controller.ts webhook path covered, createIntent (provider network call) left for P08
tests.full_unit: 1451 tests in 110 files passed; root/tooling tsc, focused ESLint, Prettier and API client drift check pass

follow_ups: P08: createIntent stores the Stripe intent ID in the clientSecret column and returns stripeIntentId to clients; review naming, idempotency and duplicate/reordered event handling (event IDs are not recorded for replay protection).
P08: decide whether STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET should be mandatory whenever STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is configured (currently the webhook fails closed at runtime).
Prisma reloads the root .env into process.env on client construction; the webhook no longer depends on it, but other module consumers listed in P01-49 still read process.env.
